51: 
52: This is **Phase 8** of the Make system-spec-kit templates and authoring docs followable by a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash agent swarm specification.

61: **Deliverables**:
62: - `scratch/scenarios.tsv`: the eight scenario rows, each with its playbook id, its file and its pass patterns.
63: - `scratch/worktree/create.out`, `create.err`, `own-code.txt`, `precondition.txt`: how the disposable worktree was made and proved.
64: - `scratch/runs/<playbook-id>.txt`: one captured run per scenario.

67: - `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/`: the report package.

71: - When this phase closes, refresh the matching file in ../changelog/ using the parent packet number plus this phase folder name.

76: <!-- ANCHOR:problem -->
77: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
78: 
79: ### Problem Statement
80: Phase 007 adds scenarios that claim the placeholder gate warns in Draft, fails at Complete, the drift guard catches a leaked description, the golden render holds, the router loads the card, the sync guard fails on drift and a DeepSeek worker can author a Level 1 packet from the card. A scenario file is a claim until someone runs its commands on a tree that contains phases 002 to 007. Without that run, phase 009 would measure templates while the playbook that describes them is untested.
81: 
82: ### Purpose
83: Every scenario this packet adds has a real execution record and a verdict that another person can check from the captured output.
84: <!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: <!-- ANCHOR:scope -->
89: ## 3. SCOPE
90: 
91: ### In Scope
92: - One disposable worktree created through `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh` from the operator's `BASE_REF`.
93: - Provisioning that worktree with its own dependency trees and its own build, proved by a realpath check.
94: - Literal execution of the eight scenarios phase 007 added, with output captured under `scratch/runs/`.
95: - A scripted compare of each run against a frozen pass pattern, with the scenario file's own Pass section as the fallback authority.
96: - At most three fix briefs and reruns for a failing scenario, then an escalation record.
97: - One report package with the real file set of an existing report folder, plus one row in the reports index.
98: - One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs.
99: 
100: ### Out of Scope
101: - Editing the scenario files. Phase 007 owns their text, and a scenario defect is escalated to its owner.
102: - Fixing product code by hand. A fix is one DeepSeek brief with one named file inside the disposable worktree.
103: - Measuring the authoring benchmark delta. Phase 009 owns that comparison.
104: - Committing or pushing. Both stay with the operator.
105: - Running anything in the primary checkout. The only scenario host is the disposable worktree.
106: 
107: ### Files to Change
108: 
109: | File Path | Change Type | Description |
110: |-----------|-------------|-------------|
111: | `scratch/scenarios.tsv`, `scratch/results.tsv`, `scratch/verdicts.md` | Create | Scenario map, verdict rows and the human-readable verdict page |
112: | `scratch/worktree/*`, `scratch/tools/*` | Create | Worktree proofs and the two runner scripts |
113: | `scratch/runs/*`, `scratch/fix/*`, `scratch/review/*` | Create | Captured runs, fix briefs and the review reply |
114: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/README.md` | Create | Report with the ten required sections |
115: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/results.csv` | Create | One row per scenario |
116: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/source.md` | Create | Where the runs and the raw evidence live |
117: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/<date>--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring/outcomes/<playbook-id>.json` | Create | One outcome record per scenario |
118: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md` | Modify | One new row at the top of the run index |
119: | `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `goal.md`, `implementation-summary.md` | Modify | Progress and evidence |
120: <!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: <!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->
125: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
126: 
127: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)
128: 
129: | ID | Requirement |
130: |----|-------------|
131: | REQ-001 | The disposable worktree is created through `worktree-naming.sh create` from `BASE_REF`, its provisioning exits 0 and the own-code check prints no `FOREIGN` line. |
132: | REQ-002 | `scratch/scenarios.tsv` holds exactly eight rows, each row names an existing scenario file and no row is a duplicate. |
133: | REQ-003 | Every scenario row has a non-empty `scratch/runs/<playbook-id>.txt` and a verdict of `PASS`, `FAIL` or `ESCALATED` in `scratch/results.tsv`. |
134: | REQ-004 | The report package holds `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and one `outcomes/<playbook-id>.json` per scenario, and `results.csv` holds eight data rows. |
135: | REQ-005 | The primary checkout status shows no change outside this phase folder, the new report folder and the one index row. When the conductor works in a build worktree, the primary checkout shows no change at all. |
136: | REQ-006 | The disposable worktree and its branch are removed after the evidence is copied, and the removal was allowed only when its status was clean or held scratch paths. |
137: 
138: ### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)
139: 
140: | ID | Requirement |
141: |----|-------------|
142: | REQ-007 | One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs ran, and each finding is applied or recorded in `goal.md` section 4 with the reason it was not. |
143: | REQ-008 | Every failed scenario has at most three fix briefs, each naming one file, and an `ESCALATED` row when the third fix did not pass. |
144: 
145: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
146: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
147: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->
148: 
149: ---
150: 
151: <!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
152: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
153: 
154: - **SC-001**: Phase 009 can read `results.csv` and know which scenarios passed without opening a run file.
155: - **SC-002**: The operator can rerun the scenario set from the report's REPRODUCIBILITY section and get the same verdicts on the same `BASE_REF`.
156: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
161: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
162: 
163: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
164: |------|------|--------|------------|
165: | Dependency | `BASE_REF` contains the phase 002 to 007 changes | Every scenario tests an old tree and fails for the wrong reason | `tasks.md` T007 checks the card, both guard scripts and the v2.3 stamp inside the disposable worktree before the first run |
166: | Dependency | The disposable worktree gets its own `node_modules` and `dist` | The run silently uses the primary checkout code | `tasks.md` T006 rejects any realpath outside the worktree and stops on `FOREIGN` |
167: | Dependency | npm can install from the registry or the local cache | Provisioning fails and no scenario can run | `worktree-naming.sh create` reports the failing package, and `tasks.md` T006 retries provisioning once, then records the blocker |
168: | Risk | A scenario file is not copy-runnable | The run fails and looks like a product defect | The failure protocol names the scenario as the owner, records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and escalates to phase 007 |
169: | Risk | Worktree removal deletes the only copy of a run | The report loses its evidence | Every run is captured under `$PHASE/scratch/runs/` in the conductor's checkout before removal, and T016 checks the count |
170: | Risk | A scenario leaves a throwaway track in the worktree | Removal is refused by the clean-status gate | The gate allows `scratch/` and `specs/zz-` paths, and T016 lists every removed path |
171: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: 
176: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
177: 
178: ### Performance
179: - **NFR-P01**: One scenario run is stopped by the runner's 30 minute alarm. A run that ends with `exit=142` is recorded as `TIMEOUT` and handled as a failure.
180: - **NFR-P02**: Provisioning the disposable worktree finishes within 45 minutes. A longer run is stopped and recorded as a blocker.
181: 
182: ### Security
183: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, a token or a key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
184: - **NFR-S02**: Every worker runs with `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` and `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0`, and its brief states the child-dispatch exemption.
185: 
186: ### Reliability
187: - **NFR-R01**: A verdict comes from a captured output file and a frozen pattern, never from a chat message. A second conductor with the same files reaches the same verdict.
188: - **NFR-R02**: The report package is written after the last run and before the worktree is removed, so no evidence depends on a deleted directory.
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ## 8. EDGE CASES
193: 
194: ### Data Boundaries
195: - Empty input: a scenario file with no `### Commands` block is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated, never executed from a guessed command.
196: - Maximum length: a run file above 2 MB is truncated to its first 2 MB and last 200 lines, and the truncation is recorded in the verdict reason.
197: - Duplicate match: two index rows that match one S label stop the map build with `AMBIGUOUS`, and no scenario runs until phase 007 is fixed.
198: 
199: ### Error Scenarios
200: - External service failure: a provider error stops the S8 dispatch. The conductor records it and retries once after 10 minutes, then marks S8 `ESCALATED`.
201: - Network timeout: a provisioning failure is retried once with `worktree-naming.sh provision`. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`.
202: - Worktree removal refused: the status gate names the offending paths. When any path is outside `scratch/` and `specs/zz-`, the worktree is kept and the operator is asked to decide.
203: 
204: ---
205: 
206: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
207: 
208: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
209: |-----------|-------|----------|
210: | Scope | 10/25 | Files: 8 scenarios read, 0 source files changed by hand. Systems: playbook, validator, guards, report index |
211: | Risk | 8/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: Y (the report index row) |
212: | Research | 8/20 | The scenario map is read from phase 007 and the report shape from an existing folder |
213: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: one runner, one S8 worker, up to three fix workers, one reviewer |
214: | Coordination | 10/15 | Dependencies: `BASE_REF`, provider login, provisioning |
215: | **Total** | **44/100** | **Level 3** |
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
220: 
221: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
222: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
223: | R-001 | A scenario passes because the worktree ran the primary checkout's code | M | M | Own-code realpath check in T006 and a `FOREIGN` stop |
224: | R-002 | A scenario fails on a real product defect and the fix worker edits the wrong file | M | M | The fix brief names the first implementation anchor from the scenario's source table and no other path |
225: | R-003 | The report is assembled from chat output rather than run files | M | L | Every report field is generated from `scratch/results.tsv` and the captured run files, and T017 reads the files |
226: | R-004 | The report index row is added twice on a rerun | L | M | T014 greps for the exact report folder name before it inserts the row |
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## 11. USER STORIES
231: 
232: ### US-001: One run per scenario (Priority: P0)
233: 
234: **As a** conductor, **I want** each scenario's own command block executed on a tree that holds every prior phase, **so that** the verdict describes the shipped behavior and not a retyped copy.
235: 
236: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ### US-002: Evidence after the worktree is gone (Priority: P0)
241: 
242: **As the** operator, **I want** every captured run and verdict to survive the disposable worktree, **so that** I can audit the phase without recreating it.
243: 
244: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
249: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
250: 
251: - None that block this phase. The one open input is the operator's `BASE_REF`, and `tasks.md` T001 stops the phase when it is absent.
252: - A scenario whose own Pass section disagrees with the frozen pass pattern is a phase 007 defect. The run records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and the phase continues with the other scenarios.
253: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## RELATED DOCUMENTS
258: 
259: - **Implementation Plan**: See `plan.md`
260: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
261: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
262: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
263: 
264: ---

142: | REQ-007 | One read-only frontier review of the report and the runs ran, and each finding is applied or recorded in `goal.md` section 4 with the reason it was not. |
143: | REQ-008 | Every failed scenario has at most three fix briefs, each naming one file, and an `ESCALATED` row when the third fix did not pass. |
144: 
145: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
146: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
147: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->
148: 
149: ---
150: 
151: <!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
152: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
153: 
154: - **SC-001**: Phase 009 can read `results.csv` and know which scenarios passed without opening a run file.
155: - **SC-002**: The operator can rerun the scenario set from the report's REPRODUCIBILITY section and get the same verdicts on the same `BASE_REF`.
156: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
161: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
162: 
163: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
164: |------|------|--------|------------|
165: | Dependency | `BASE_REF` contains the phase 002 to 007 changes | Every scenario tests an old tree and fails for the wrong reason | `tasks.md` T007 checks the card, both guard scripts and the v2.3 stamp inside the disposable worktree before the first run |
166: | Dependency | The disposable worktree gets its own `node_modules` and `dist` | The run silently uses the primary checkout code | `tasks.md` T006 rejects any realpath outside the worktree and stops on `FOREIGN` |
167: | Dependency | npm can install from the registry or the local cache | Provisioning fails and no scenario can run | `worktree-naming.sh create` reports the failing package, and `tasks.md` T006 retries provisioning once, then records the blocker |
168: | Risk | A scenario file is not copy-runnable | The run fails and looks like a product defect | The failure protocol names the scenario as the owner, records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and escalates to phase 007 |
169: | Risk | Worktree removal deletes the only copy of a run | The report loses its evidence | Every run is captured under `$PHASE/scratch/runs/` in the conductor's checkout before removal, and T016 checks the count |
170: | Risk | A scenario leaves a throwaway track in the worktree | Removal is refused by the clean-status gate | The gate allows `scratch/` and `specs/zz-` paths, and T016 lists every removed path |
171: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: 
176: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
177: 
178: ### Performance
179: - **NFR-P01**: One scenario run is stopped by the runner's 30 minute alarm. A run that ends with `exit=142` is recorded as `TIMEOUT` and handled as a failure.
180: - **NFR-P02**: Provisioning the disposable worktree finishes within 45 minutes. A longer run is stopped and recorded as a blocker.
181: 
182: ### Security
183: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, a token or a key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
184: - **NFR-S02**: Every worker runs with `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` and `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0`, and its brief states the child-dispatch exemption.
185: 
186: ### Reliability
187: - **NFR-R01**: A verdict comes from a captured output file and a frozen pattern, never from a chat message. A second conductor with the same files reaches the same verdict.
188: - **NFR-R02**: The report package is written after the last run and before the worktree is removed, so no evidence depends on a deleted directory.
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ## 8. EDGE CASES
193: 
194: ### Data Boundaries
195: - Empty input: a scenario file with no `### Commands` block is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated, never executed from a guessed command.
196: - Maximum length: a run file above 2 MB is truncated to its first 2 MB and last 200 lines, and the truncation is recorded in the verdict reason.
197: - Duplicate match: two index rows that match one S label stop the map build with `AMBIGUOUS`, and no scenario runs until phase 007 is fixed.
198: 
199: ### Error Scenarios
200: - External service failure: a provider error stops the S8 dispatch. The conductor records it and retries once after 10 minutes, then marks S8 `ESCALATED`.
201: - Network timeout: a provisioning failure is retried once with `worktree-naming.sh provision`. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`.
202: - Worktree removal refused: the status gate names the offending paths. When any path is outside `scratch/` and `specs/zz-`, the worktree is kept and the operator is asked to decide.
203: 
204: ---
205: 
206: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
207: 
208: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
209: |-----------|-------|----------|
210: | Scope | 10/25 | Files: 8 scenarios read, 0 source files changed by hand. Systems: playbook, validator, guards, report index |
211: | Risk | 8/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: Y (the report index row) |
212: | Research | 8/20 | The scenario map is read from phase 007 and the report shape from an existing folder |
213: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: one runner, one S8 worker, up to three fix workers, one reviewer |
214: | Coordination | 10/15 | Dependencies: `BASE_REF`, provider login, provisioning |
215: | **Total** | **44/100** | **Level 3** |
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
220: 
221: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
222: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
223: | R-001 | A scenario passes because the worktree ran the primary checkout's code | M | M | Own-code realpath check in T006 and a `FOREIGN` stop |
224: | R-002 | A scenario fails on a real product defect and the fix worker edits the wrong file | M | M | The fix brief names the first implementation anchor from the scenario's source table and no other path |
225: | R-003 | The report is assembled from chat output rather than run files | M | L | Every report field is generated from `scratch/results.tsv` and the captured run files, and T017 reads the files |
226: | R-004 | The report index row is added twice on a rerun | L | M | T014 greps for the exact report folder name before it inserts the row |
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## 11. USER STORIES
231: 
232: ### US-001: One run per scenario (Priority: P0)
233: 
234: **As a** conductor, **I want** each scenario's own command block executed on a tree that holds every prior phase, **so that** the verdict describes the shipped behavior and not a retyped copy.
235: 
236: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ### US-002: Evidence after the worktree is gone (Priority: P0)
241: 
242: **As the** operator, **I want** every captured run and verdict to survive the disposable worktree, **so that** I can audit the phase without recreating it.
243: 
244: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
249: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
250: 
251: - None that block this phase. The one open input is the operator's `BASE_REF`, and `tasks.md` T001 stops the phase when it is absent.
252: - A scenario whose own Pass section disagrees with the frozen pass pattern is a phase 007 defect. The run records `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and the phase continues with the other scenarios.
253: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->

### Prompt

Scaffold a Level 2 packet, leave the value tokens unfilled, and tell me whether strict validation still passes while the packet is a Draft.

Run the commands from the checkout root in one shell session, so the variables set in step 1 stay defined.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: Worktree/Branch Naming Allocator + Validator
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two flat, spec-style numbered namespaces keep a Git-UI branch tree legible as
# a few clean folders instead of a per-skill pile. A worktree-backed branch
# lives under worktrees/, a dedicated worktree-less branch under branches/,
# both numbered 001, 002, 003 … strictly sequentially with no skipped or
# reused number. skilled/ (releases) and backup/ (safety refs) stay.
#
#   WORKTREE_BRANCH := "worktrees/" NNN "-" SLUG    (NNN 3-digit 001..999)
#   WORKTREE_DIR    := BASE "/" NNN "-" SLUG         (dir mirrors the branch tail)
#   BASE            := speckit.worktreeBase | $SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE | ".worktrees"
#                       (default keeps the tree in-checkout; a configured base
#                        moves it OUT so the checkout's file-watchers — Git
#                        status/fsmonitor, GUIs, sync clients — stop scanning
#                        every worktree's node_modules)
#   DEDICATED_BRANCH:= "branches/" NNN "-" SLUG      (a branch with NO worktree)
#   RELEASE         := "skilled/v" A "." B "." C "." D
#   BACKUP          := "backup/" ANYTHING            (safety refs; legal, not numbered)
#   RESERVED        := "main"
#   WRAPPER         := "work/" RUNTIME "/" SLUG      (launch-wrapper lane; exempt)
#   SLUG            := lowercase [a-z0-9-], no leading/trailing/double hyphen
#
# worktrees/ and branches/ each own an INDEPENDENT 001-based sequence (like two
# spec tracks), so a worktrees/003 and a branches/003 may coexist. Git cannot
# enforce sequential numbering itself, so allocation holds a lock in the shared
# common Git dir and seeds its max from the namespace's stored high-water mark,
# every matching local + remote ref, and (for worktrees/) every registered
# worktree's NNN-* basename (location-independent, so relocating the base never
# lets a number be reissued) — a partial scan can never reissue a live number.
# Gaps are never back-filled: next = max-in-use + 1, even after a delete.
#
# Sourceable: validators (is_valid_slug/nnn/branch/wrapper/backup/pair) are
# used by the pre-push hook. Strict mode is scoped to direct execution so
# sourcing a caller's shell does not inherit `set -e`.

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "${0}" ]]; then
  set -euo pipefail
fi

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. REPO RESOLUTION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_wn_common_dir() { git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null; }

# The common dir's parent is the main worktree toplevel (works from any linked
# worktree, so the counters are shared clone-wide rather than per-worktree).
_wn_toplevel() {
  local common
  common="$(_wn_common_dir)" || return 1
  [ -n "$common" ] || return 1
  ( cd "$(dirname "$common")" && pwd -P )
}

# Absolute directory that holds worktrees/NNN-slug working trees. Kept
# configurable so the trees can live OUTSIDE the primary checkout: with dozens
# of nested worktrees the checkout's own file-watchers (Git status/fsmonitor,
# GUIs, sync clients) otherwise walk every worktree's node_modules on each scan.
# Precedence: env SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE > git config speckit.worktreeBase >
# default "<toplevel>/.worktrees" (unchanged legacy behavior when neither is
# set, so other clones and tests keep the in-checkout layout). A relative value
# resolves against the main toplevel; a leading ~ expands to $HOME.
_wn_base_dir() {
  local top raw
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || return 1
  raw="${SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE:-$(git -C "$top" config --get speckit.worktreeBase 2>/dev/null || true)}"
  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw=".worktrees"
  case "$raw" in
    "~")   raw="$HOME" ;;
    "~/"*) raw="$HOME/${raw#\~/}" ;;
  esac
  case "$raw" in
    /*) printf '%s\n' "$raw" ;;
    *)  printf '%s\n' "$top/$raw" ;;
  esac
}

# Per-namespace high-water files keep the two counters independent.
_wn_highwater_file() { echo "$(_wn_common_dir)/$1-number.highwater"; }
_wn_lock_dir()       { echo "$(_wn_common_dir)/worktree-number.lock"; }

_wn_valid_namespace() { [ "$1" = "worktrees" ] || [ "$1" = "branches" ]; }

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. VALIDATORS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_valid_slug() {
  local s="$1"
  case "$s" in
    ""|*[!a-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;;   # only lowercase letters, digits, hyphen
    -*|*-|*--*)      return 1 ;;   # no leading/trailing/double hyphen
  esac
  return 0
}

# Exactly 3 digits, value 001..999, interpreted base-10 (leading zeros are not
# octal — 007 is the number 7, not octal 7 == 7, but 099 must not trip octal).
is_valid_nnn() {
  local n="${1:-}" value
  case "$n" in [0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  value=$((10#$n))
  [[ "$value" -ge 1 && "$value" -le 999 ]]
}

# Legal, in-grammar branch: reserved, release, a numbered worktrees/ or
# branches/ task branch, or one of the two legal-but-not-task lanes (wrapper
# and backup). Owner-first and malformed names are rejected.
is_valid_branch() {
  local b="$1"
  [ "$b" = "main" ] && return 0
  if [[ "$b" =~ ^skilled/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then return 0; fi
  is_wrapper_branch "$b" && return 0
  is_backup_branch  "$b" && return 0
  if [[ "$b" =~ ^(worktrees|branches)/([0-9][0-9][0-9])-([a-z0-9-]+)$ ]]; then
    is_valid_nnn "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" || return 1
    is_valid_slug "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" || return 1
    return 0

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. VALIDATORS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_valid_slug() {
  local s="$1"
  case "$s" in
    ""|*[!a-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;;   # only lowercase letters, digits, hyphen
    -*|*-|*--*)      return 1 ;;   # no leading/trailing/double hyphen
  esac
  return 0
}

# Exactly 3 digits, value 001..999, interpreted base-10 (leading zeros are not
# octal — 007 is the number 7, not octal 7 == 7, but 099 must not trip octal).
is_valid_nnn() {
  local n="${1:-}" value
  case "$n" in [0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  value=$((10#$n))
  [[ "$value" -ge 1 && "$value" -le 999 ]]
}

# Legal, in-grammar branch: reserved, release, a numbered worktrees/ or
# branches/ task branch, or one of the two legal-but-not-task lanes (wrapper
# and backup). Owner-first and malformed names are rejected.
is_valid_branch() {
  local b="$1"
  [ "$b" = "main" ] && return 0
  if [[ "$b" =~ ^skilled/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then return 0; fi
  is_wrapper_branch "$b" && return 0
  is_backup_branch  "$b" && return 0
  if [[ "$b" =~ ^(worktrees|branches)/([0-9][0-9][0-9])-([a-z0-9-]+)$ ]]; then
    is_valid_nnn "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" || return 1
    is_valid_slug "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" || return 1
    return 0

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 4. BRANCH / WORKTREE CREATION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_wn_default_base() {
  echo "${SPECKIT_LIVE_BRANCH:-$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)}"
}

# create_named_worktree <slug> [base] — allocate a worktrees/ number, then
# create branch worktrees/NNN-slug and directory .worktrees/NNN-slug together.
# Emits "<branch> <dir>" on success.
# Returns 3 when the worktree was created but provisioning failed.
create_named_worktree() {
  local slug="" base="" provision=1 arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
      --no-provision) provision=0 ;;
      *) if [ -z "$slug" ]; then slug="$arg"; elif [ -z "$base" ]; then base="$arg"; fi ;;
    esac
  done
  local top wtbase nnn branch dir provision_rc=0
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  wtbase="$(_wn_base_dir)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree base" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number worktrees)" || return 1
  branch="worktrees/$nnn-$slug"
  dir="$wtbase/$nnn-$slug"
  mkdir -p "$wtbase" || { echo "cannot create worktree base: $wtbase" >&2; return 1; }
  git -C "$top" worktree add -b "$branch" "$dir" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  # A worktree nobody can build is not a worktree anybody wanted.
  if [ "$provision" = "1" ]; then
    if ! provision_worktree "$dir"; then
      echo "worktree created but provisioning failed: $dir; run: worktree-naming.sh provision $dir" >&2
      provision_rc=3
    fi
  fi
  echo "$branch $dir"
  return "$provision_rc"
}

# create_branch <slug> [base] — allocate a branches/ number and create branch
# branches/NNN-slug WITHOUT a worktree. Emits the branch name on success.
create_branch() {
  local slug="$1" base="${2:-}" top nnn branch
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number branches)" || return 1
  branch="branches/$nnn-$slug"
  git -C "$top" branch "$branch" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  echo "$branch"
}

# create_detached_worktree <slug> [base] — numbered dir, no branch. Uses the
# worktrees/ counter so a detached dir can never collide with a paired one.
create_detached_worktree() {
  local slug="$1" base="${2:-}" top wtbase nnn dir
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  wtbase="$(_wn_base_dir)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree base" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number worktrees)" || return 1
  dir="$wtbase/$nnn-detached-$slug"
  mkdir -p "$wtbase" || { echo "cannot create worktree base: $wtbase" >&2; return 1; }
  git -C "$top" worktree add --detach "$dir" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  echo "$dir"
}

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 4b. DEPENDENCY PROVISIONING
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every dependency tree in this repository is gitignored, so a worktree starts
# with none of them. Unprovisioned, it does not fail cleanly: a build can exit 0
# having compiled nothing, and a conformance check that copies a skill hub into

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 4. BRANCH / WORKTREE CREATION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_wn_default_base() {
  echo "${SPECKIT_LIVE_BRANCH:-$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)}"
}

# create_named_worktree <slug> [base] — allocate a worktrees/ number, then
# create branch worktrees/NNN-slug and directory .worktrees/NNN-slug together.
# Emits "<branch> <dir>" on success.
# Returns 3 when the worktree was created but provisioning failed.
create_named_worktree() {
  local slug="" base="" provision=1 arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
      --no-provision) provision=0 ;;
      *) if [ -z "$slug" ]; then slug="$arg"; elif [ -z "$base" ]; then base="$arg"; fi ;;
    esac
  done
  local top wtbase nnn branch dir provision_rc=0
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  wtbase="$(_wn_base_dir)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree base" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number worktrees)" || return 1
  branch="worktrees/$nnn-$slug"
  dir="$wtbase/$nnn-$slug"
  mkdir -p "$wtbase" || { echo "cannot create worktree base: $wtbase" >&2; return 1; }
  git -C "$top" worktree add -b "$branch" "$dir" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  # A worktree nobody can build is not a worktree anybody wanted.
  if [ "$provision" = "1" ]; then
    if ! provision_worktree "$dir"; then
      echo "worktree created but provisioning failed: $dir; run: worktree-naming.sh provision $dir" >&2
      provision_rc=3
    fi
  fi
  echo "$branch $dir"
  return "$provision_rc"
}

# create_branch <slug> [base] — allocate a branches/ number and create branch
# branches/NNN-slug WITHOUT a worktree. Emits the branch name on success.
create_branch() {
  local slug="$1" base="${2:-}" top nnn branch
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number branches)" || return 1
  branch="branches/$nnn-$slug"
  git -C "$top" branch "$branch" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  echo "$branch"
}

# create_detached_worktree <slug> [base] — numbered dir, no branch. Uses the
# worktrees/ counter so a detached dir can never collide with a paired one.
create_detached_worktree() {
  local slug="$1" base="${2:-}" top wtbase nnn dir
  is_valid_slug "$slug" || { echo "invalid slug: $slug" >&2; return 1; }
  top="$(_wn_toplevel)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  wtbase="$(_wn_base_dir)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree base" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -n "$base" ] || base="$(_wn_default_base)"
  nnn="$(allocate_number worktrees)" || return 1
  dir="$wtbase/$nnn-detached-$slug"
  mkdir -p "$wtbase" || { echo "cannot create worktree base: $wtbase" >&2; return 1; }
  git -C "$top" worktree add --detach "$dir" "$base" >&2 || return 1
  echo "$dir"
}

The one file a fix may touch is the `- Implementation:` bullet of the scenario file's `## 4. SOURCE FILES` list. The conductor resolves that link against the scenario file's own directory, prints the result as `FIX_TARGET=<repo-relative path>` and copies that path into the brief and into ALLOWED WRITE PATHS. No second file is allowed. A scenario with no `- Implementation:` bullet is `SCENARIO_DEFECT`.

The fix brief is the skeleton in the AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL section, followed by this text with the fields filled:

```text
TASK: Scenario <S label> failed at <playbook id>.
The captured run is <run file>. The comparator wrote:
<the contents of <run file>.check.txt, quoted>
The scenario's pass criterion is:
<the Pass line from the scenario file, quoted>
Change only the single file named under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS so that the scenario
passes. Do not edit the scenario file. Do not edit any other file.
The conductor reruns the scenario after you return.
RETURN exactly one line: FIXED <the file> or BLOCKED <the reason>
```

After the worker returns, the conductor reruns the same scenario command block from `$WT`. A PASS marks the row `FIXED` and keeps the original run beside the rerun as `scratch/runs/<playbook-id>.fix-<n>.txt`.

A fix edits a tracked file under `.skilled/`, so the disposable worktree is never clean after a successful fix. Before removal, T016 saves the worktree state:

```bash
git -C "$WT" diff > "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/fix.patch"
git -C "$WT" status --porcelain > "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/status.txt"
```

The removal gate then reads `status.txt` line by line and looks for `diff --git a/<path> b/<path>` in `fix.patch`. It writes `PATCHED <path>` or `UNPATCHED <path>` for each change, prints `PATCH_GATE_COVERED` when the counts agree, and refuses removal while any `UNPATCHED` line exists. The patch is applied to the build worktree later by the operator or the phase 009 conductor, never by this phase.

perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 1800 bash "$out.cmd" > "$out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
size=$(wc -c < "$out" | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$size" -gt 2097152 ]; then
  { head -c 2097152 "$out"; printf '\n[truncated]\n'; tail -n 200 "$out"; } > "$out.trunc"
  mv "$out.trunc" "$out"
  printf 'truncated=yes\n' >> "$out"
else
  printf 'truncated=no\n' >> "$out"
fi
printf 'exit=%s\n' "$rc" >> "$out"
exit 0

- [ ] T010 Run S8 as a DeepSeek authoring dispatch (`scratch/briefs/S8.txt`, `scratch/runs/<S8 id>.txt`). Read the shared skeleton, extract the scenario prompt, assemble the brief, then run the block below. Each worker transcript is saved as `scratch/runs/<S8 id>.worker-<n>.jsonl` and the run file holds conductor-written lines only, so a `RESULT: PASSED` line inside the transcript can never satisfy the S8 pattern. A provider error is retried once after 10 minutes, and a second failure marks S8 `ESCALATED`. Verify: `test -s "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt" && echo S8_RUN_OK` prints `S8_RUN_OK`, `rg -c '^RESULT: PASSED$' "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt"` prints `1`, `rg -c '^leftover_tokens 0$' "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt"` prints `1`, `rg -c '^dispatch_exit=0$' "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt"` prints `1` and `rg -c '^S8\tPASS\t' "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"` prints `1`. When the packet is missing, the worker did not follow the frozen path: append `S8 FAIL <S8 id> <run file>` as four tab-separated fields to the results file and run T011. When the second dispatch also fails, the block prints `S8_ESCALATED`, writes the first error line in `goal.md` section 4 and appends the `ESCALATED` row.

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
RUNROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
PHASE="$RUNROOT/specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree"
source "$PHASE/scratch/env.sh"
S8_ID=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="S8"{print $2}' "$PHASE/scratch/scenarios.tsv")
S8_FILE=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="S8"{print $3}' "$PHASE/scratch/scenarios.tsv")
cat >> "$PHASE/scratch/env.sh" <<EOF
S8_ID="$S8_ID"
S8_FILE="$S8_FILE"
EOF
awk '/^### Prompt/{f=1;next} f&&/^```/{if(b){exit}else{b=1;next}} f&&b{print}' "$S8_FILE" > "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/S8-prompt.txt"
test -s "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/skeleton.txt" && echo SKELETON_OK
{
  cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/skeleton.txt"
  printf '\nTASK: Author one Level 1 spec packet from the authoring card, following the scenario\nprompt below exactly.\n\n'
  cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/S8-prompt.txt"
  printf '\n\nSteps:\n1. Read .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md once.\n2. Run: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --skip-branch --level 1 --track zz-pb-card --short-name card-authoring --number 1 "Author a Level 1 packet from the card"\n3. Fill spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and implementation-summary.md for this feature: add a --quiet flag to .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh that prints only the final recommended-level line.\n4. Run: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring --strict\n5. Fix what it reports and run it again, at most three times in all.\n\nRETURN exactly one line: the folder path, then the last RESULT line validate.sh printed.\n'
} > "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/S8.txt"
RC=1
ATTEMPT=0
for N in 1 2; do
  ATTEMPT=$N
  ( cd "$WT" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
      -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
      "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/S8.txt")" ) </dev/null \
      > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.worker-$N.jsonl" 2>&1
  RC=$?
  [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && break
  rg -qi 'provider|rate limit|overloaded|unavailable|timeout|503|529' "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.worker-$N.jsonl" || break
  [ "$N" -eq 1 ] && { echo "provider_error=$RC"; sleep 600; }
done
P="$WT/specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring"
LEFT=unknown
{
  printf 'dispatch_exit=%s\n' "$RC"
  printf 'dispatch_attempts=%s\n' "$ATTEMPT"
  echo "--- conductor validation ---"
  if [ -d "$P" ]; then
    ( cd "$WT" && bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh "$P" --strict ) 2>&1
    LEFT=$(rg -o 'YOUR_VALUE_HERE:|NEEDS CLARIFICATION:' "$P" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    printf 'leftover_tokens %s\n' "$LEFT"
  else
    echo "MISSING $P"
    echo "leftover_tokens unknown"
  fi
  echo "--- end conductor validation ---"
} > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt"
rm -r "$WT/specs/zz-pb-card" 2>/dev/null || true
[ ! -d "$WT/specs/zz-pb-card" ] && echo "cleanup=ok" >> "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt"
awk -F'\t' '$1 != "S8"' "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv" > "$PHASE/scratch/results.tmp"
mv "$PHASE/scratch/results.tmp" "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
LINE=$(node "$PHASE/scratch/tools/check-run.cjs" "$PHASE/scratch/scenarios.tsv" S8 "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt")
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$LEFT" = "0" ] && printf '%s' "$LINE" | grep -q 'PASS'; then
  printf '%s\n' "$LINE" >> "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
  echo S8_PASS
elif [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  printf 'S8\tESCALATED\t%s\t%s\n' "$S8_ID" "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.worker-$ATTEMPT.jsonl" >> "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
  ERR=$(rg -m1 -i 'provider|rate limit|overloaded|unavailable|timeout|503|529' "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.worker-$ATTEMPT.jsonl" | cut -c1-200)
  printf 'S8 ESCALATED provider error after %s dispatch attempts: %s\n' "$ATTEMPT" "$ERR" >> "$PHASE/goal.md"
  echo S8_ESCALATED
else
  printf 'S8\tFAIL\t%s\t%s\n' "$S8_ID" "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$S8_ID.txt" >> "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
  echo "leftover_tokens=$LEFT"
fi
tail -1 "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
```

  LATEST="$PHASE/scratch/runs/$ID.fix-$N.txt"

- [ ] T016 Save the worktree diff, check the evidence and remove the disposable worktree and its branch (`scratch/fixes/fix.patch`, `scratch/fixes/status.txt`, `scratch/worktree/removal.txt`). Run the block below. It prints `RUNS_RECORDED 8` only when eight verdict rows exist and every evidence file is non-empty. It then saves the worktree diff and status, writes `PATCHED` or `UNPATCHED` for every changed path and prints `PATCH_GATE_COVERED` when the two counts agree. Verify: the block prints `RUNS_RECORDED 8`, `PATCH_GATE_COVERED`, `REMOVAL_OK`, `WORKTREE_GONE` and `BRANCH_GONE`. A `NO_ROWS`, `EMPTY <label>` or `UNPATCHED <path>` line stops the removal with `REMOVAL_REFUSED`, keeps the worktree and must be recorded in `goal.md` section 4. The rollback sentence is in `plan.md` section 7. Removal is irreversible for uncommitted files in the worktree.

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
RUNROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
PHASE="$RUNROOT/specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree"
source "$PHASE/scratch/env.sh"
mkdir -p "$PHASE/scratch/fixes"
{
  ROWS=$(wc -l < "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv" | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$ROWS" = "8" ] && echo "RUNS_RECORDED 8" || echo "NO_ROWS $ROWS"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r LABEL ID VERDICT RUN; do
    test -s "$RUN" || echo "EMPTY $LABEL"
  done < "$PHASE/scratch/results.tsv"
} > "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/evidence-before-remove.txt"
git -C "$WT" diff > "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/fix.patch"
git -C "$WT" status --porcelain > "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/status.txt"
: > "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"
while read -r XY PATHSPEC; do
  [ -z "${PATHSPEC:-}" ] && continue
  if grep -qF "diff --git a/$PATHSPEC b/$PATHSPEC" "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/fix.patch"; then
    printf 'PATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"
  else
    printf 'UNPATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"
  fi
done < "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/status.txt"
STATUS_N=$(grep -c . "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/status.txt" || true)
PATCHED_N=$(grep -c '^PATCHED ' "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt" || true)
[ "$STATUS_N" = "$PATCHED_N" ] && echo PATCH_GATE_COVERED >> "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"
{
  cat "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/evidence-before-remove.txt"
  cat "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"
  if rg -q '^(NO_ROWS|EMPTY|UNPATCHED) ' "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/evidence-before-remove.txt" "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"; then
    echo REMOVAL_REFUSED
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! rg -q '^PATCH_GATE_COVERED$' "$PHASE/scratch/fixes/gate.txt"; then
    echo REMOVAL_REFUSED
    exit 1
  fi
  echo REMOVAL_OK
  git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree remove --force "$WT"
  git -C "$RUNROOT" branch -D "$WT_BRANCH"
  test ! -d "$WT" && echo WORKTREE_GONE
  git -C "$RUNROOT" branch --list "$WT_BRANCH" | grep -q . || echo BRANCH_GONE
} 2>&1 | tee "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/removal.txt"
```

set -eu
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'diff --git a/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh b/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh\n' > "$TMP/fix.patch"
printf ' M .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh\n' > "$TMP/status.txt"
: > "$TMP/gate.txt"
while read -r XY PATHSPEC; do
  [ -z "${PATHSPEC:-}" ] && continue
  if grep -qF "diff --git a/$PATHSPEC b/$PATHSPEC" "$TMP/fix.patch"; then printf 'PATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$TMP/gate.txt"; else printf 'UNPATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$TMP/gate.txt"; fi
done < "$TMP/status.txt"
printf '?? specs/zz-pb-card/001-card-authoring/\n' >> "$TMP/status.txt"
: > "$TMP/gate2.txt"
while read -r XY PATHSPEC; do
  [ -z "${PATHSPEC:-}" ] && continue
  if grep -qF "diff --git a/$PATHSPEC b/$PATHSPEC" "$TMP/fix.patch"; then printf 'PATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$TMP/gate2.txt"; else printf 'UNPATCHED %s\n' "$PATHSPEC" >> "$TMP/gate2.txt"; fi
done < "$TMP/status.txt"
echo '--- case 1:'; cat "$TMP/gate.txt"
